svg.text: The building is locked. Every tile is the same architecture receiving a different act of care — paint, plants, light, signage, furniture. Charm from care, not clutter.
massing, roofs, windows, proportions: unchanged in every tile
S-06/S-07 undressed — the yardstick every treatment answers to
number, porch light, doormat, two pots — the smallest act of pride
planted timber boxes under three cills; flowers in the accent family
one plant trained up the corner on wires — care visible in the training
low brick wall, timber gate on the door axis, path, two shrubs
painted gutters and downpipe, soldier courses, chimney pots, an aerial
lit rooms, a porch lamp, a wall lantern, one street lamp — home at dusk
striped awning, painted fascia, one table and two stools, an A-board
painted fascia, hanging sign on an iron bracket, lantern, planted pots
pillar box, parish notice board, painted fascia — the civic version
a bench, a leaning bicycle, a lamp post — life implied, no people
door + boxes + gutters + pots + a bicycle — several small acts, one home
“I’d love to live there” — not “that’s a cute stylized building.” Warmth, optimism and craftsmanship; never caricature.
SHEET 02 FOUND THE VOICE · SHEET 03 MAKES IT LOVABLE
every treatment is reversible dressing on the locked language — nothing here touches the architecture

LEAD’S VERDICT — strongest three: L-02 THE FRONT DOOR (love legible at the threshold; a kit every resident can vary) · L-03 WINDOW BOXES (colour with a reason; reads at any distance) · L-06 CRAFT (care in the fabric itself — gutters, courses, pots).

RECOMMENDED — L-12 LIVED-IN, which is exactly those three combined: the entrance kit on every home, boxes on one or two windows, the craft layer everywhere. Garden, street and shop kits deploy by context, not by default.

WHY IT WORKS — every element is evidence of a caring hand rather than applied cuteness, and every one is a per-resident variable the simulation can own — so the town dresses itself differently on every street.
